10102.name: SHELL_READY
10102.meaning: Every Clubhouse page opens in the frame: on wide screens the sidebar, the top bar with the bell and the page; on a phone the page with the role's tab bar and More sheet.

10103.name: TEAM_SWITCH_READS_EVERY_SCREEN_AGAIN
10103.meaning: Switching teams sets the active team on the server (the same action Fairway uses), then refreshes the page so the layout, the sidebar's next event and Roster badge, and the page itself read for the new team; the route remounts for the new team, so a search, an open panel or a live feed the old team's screen held does not carry over, while a refresh for the same team keeps its state.

10201.name: THE_BELL_IS_LOADING_ITS_LIST
10201.meaning: The bell is loading its list

catalogRow.theySee: Four skeleton rows; a warm list stays on screen while it refreshes

10202.name: A_PHONE_PAGE_OPENED_FROM_MORE_OR
10202.meaning: A phone page opened from More, a page below another (a qualifier, its selections, a round, recovery), or a coach's full-page form (a new or edited qualifier) is loading or still arriving from the server

catalogRow.theySee: Its top bar is already the pushed bar: the back link named for where it goes ("‹ More", "‹ Qualifiers", a form's plain Cancel) and the page's title, where the page's own bar draws them, never the tab root's title and bell; the page's bar replaces it in place, adding its action (WebKit 390, 2026-10-08: back link and title moved 0px from loading to loaded on 14 routes). The address's query decides two bars: a Settings section (`?section=`, or an old Settings address) goes back to Settings, and a coach's player on Stats (`?player=`) goes back to the team. A full-screen flow (the coach's qualifier forms, a player's new round and the round itself) hides the tab bar from its first frame, as its page does once it is up. Back works while it loads. Settings keeps the bar's title for VoiceOver only, as its page does. A page that draws a tab root's title (the player's Messages) or its own chrome (a new round, the round itself), the coach's pages a player meets only as the coach-only notice, and an address not rebuilt for the role keep the plain bar
catalogRow.how: `phonePushedTop` and `phoneFullScreen` (shell/nav.ts) into `TopBar` as `PushedTopStandIn` (shell/phone-chrome.tsx) and `FrameRoot`; the query from `ClubhouseShell` (`useSearchParams`); `PhoneTop` and the chrome hooks take hold in a layout effect, in the page's own commit

10301.name: BELL_REFRESHES_ON_OPEN
10301.meaning: The bell reads its list again every time it opens; a list already shown stays on screen while the new one loads.

10401.name: A_PAGE_THAT_HASNT_BEEN_REBUILT_IN
10401.meaning: A page that hasn't been rebuilt in Clubhouse

catalogRow.theySee: The page empty's anatomy, as the route error draws it, with no card: an hourglass medallion, "Rounds hasn’t been rebuilt yet", one sentence, and Back to Home. A player on a page rebuilt for coaches only (Recruiting, What's new): a lock, "Only coaches use Recruiting", "Your rounds, stats and team are on Home." and Back to Home  An old address on its way to its new screen draws that screen's skeleton (the plain page skeleton when the destination isn't known) while it redirects, and keeps waiting while its segment still streams; this page shows only once the segment rendered without redirecting (GAP-S-19)
The shared section empty at the rows' inset: "You’re all caught up" + what shows up here
The shared section empty: "Nothing of this kind" + Show all

10406.name: A_DASHBOARD_URL_THAT_MATCHES_NOTHING_OR

Everything else is where you left it.", and one way back: to the section ("Back to Practice", "Back to Drills") or Back to Home. catalogRow.how: `ClubhouseNotFound` (`shell/NotFound.tsx`, `thing`, `back`) from `dashboard/not-found.tsx` and the section not-found files (`practice/not-found.tsx`, `practice/plan/[planId]`, `practice/print/[planId]`, `practice/drills/[drillId]`). "Notifications didn’t load" + "Try again; the error has been reported." inside the panel, at the rows' inset. The panel's head drops its unread count and Mark all read until the list loads (the bell keeps its count)

10603.name: THE_PAGE_WAS_BUILT_FOR_AN_OLDER
10603.meaning: The page was built for an older version

10604.name: GOLFHELM_UPDATED_WHILE_THE_PAGE_WAS_OPEN
10604.meaning: GolfHelm updated while the page was open

"GolfHelm is slow to respond" + "GolfHelm didn’t answer in time. Nothing you saved is lost. Try again." (no guessed cause, B10.3). Try again

The page named from the boundary's `route` ("Rounds didn’t load": its nav item, else its first segment as words); "This page didn’t finish loading" for Home or a route outside the dashboard. "Nothing you saved is lost. Try again.", with no guess at the cause (row 62). Try again

The page named from the boundary's `route`, as CH-1205 ("Rounds didn’t load"), or "Something went wrong on this page" for Home or a route outside the dashboard, + "Nothing you saved is lost. Try again." (never "reported automatically", B10.3); Try again first, then the way back the route's boundary names (`homePath`): Back to Home, or its section for a sub-screen, such as Back to Rounds; the error's reference as a quiet caption ("Reference …"), never in a card

10608.name: THE_SIDEBARS_NEXT_EVENT_DOESNT_LOAD

10609.name: THE_ROSTER_BADGES_JOIN_REQUESTS_DONT_LOAD

10610.name: SIGNING_OUT_FROM_THE_PHONES_MORE_SHEET
10610.meaning: Signing out from the phone's account sheet fails

10611.name: SWITCHING_TEAM_FAILS
10611.meaning: Switching team fails (a head coach on more than one team)

catalogRow.theySee: "Couldn't switch to UNCW Women's Golf" + why when the server said ("Only a head coach staffed on more than one team can switch.", "You aren't staffed on that team.", "Your session ended. Sign in again.") with no Retry, or "You're still on UNCW Men's Golf. Try again." with Retry when it was the network; error haptic. The team on screen goes back to the one they were on
catalogRow.how: `useTeamSwitch` → `useAction('shell.switchTeam')` over `setActiveTeam`; the bell opening another team's item (`Bell` `openOnTeam`, or at once when the coach can't switch)

10612.name: TWO_OR_MORE_PARTS_OF_A_PAGE
10612.meaning: Two or more parts of a page don't load

catalogRow.theySee: One notice under the page head, "Some of this page didn’t load", naming the parts in one sentence ("This week’s schedule, recent rounds and the leaderboard didn’t load. Nothing you saved is lost. Try again."), with one Try again that re-runs the page. Each failed part keeps its heading and only its notice's title (covered), with no button and no second alert. One part failing keeps that part's own notice
catalogRow.how: `PageNotice`, `PageRefreshNotice`; `covered` on `InlineNotice` and `RefreshNotice`; the page passes the parts its render knows failed. In use on Home (coach and player, desktop and phone), Team stats (desktop and phone), the Roster (desktop and phone) and the Team Hub

10613.name: TWO_OR_MORE_SECTIONS_OF_A_PAGE
10613.meaning: Two or more sections of a page crash in the browser

catalogRow.theySee: One notice under the page head, "Some of this page couldn’t be shown", naming the sections in reading order ("Team figures, the trend chart and season bests couldn’t be shown. The rest of the page is fine. Try again."), with one Try again that tries every one of them again. Each crashed section keeps only its notice's title (covered). One crash keeps its own notice and Try again; a section that fails again after Try again is told again. Each crash is still reported on its own surface
catalogRow.how: `SectionGroup` around the page's one rendered tree, `SectionGroupNotice` under its head (ui/SectionBoundary.tsx); browser-only, so the server HTML has none of it

10614.name: A_PAGES_ONE_READ_DOESNT_LOAD_SO
10614.meaning: A page's one read doesn't load, so nothing can show under its head

catalogRow.theySee: The page empty in the danger tone, as the route error draws it: a brick medallion, the title and one or two sentences, Try again first (it re-runs the page), then the page's own action; an alert. Offline, Try again says so instead (CH-1905). The page passes its own number
catalogRow.how: `EmptyState size="page" tone="danger"` with `PageRetry` (ui/Retry.tsx). In use on Team stats for CH-4201 (desktop and phone)

10615.name: DELIVER_NOW_IN_THE_BELL_IS_REFUSED
10615.meaning: Deliver now in the bell is refused (P-10)

catalogRow.theySee: A toast "Couldn’t deliver them" + "They will arrive when class ends. Try again."; the row stays

10616.name: A_PLAYERS_PUSHES_ARE_HELD_FOR_CLASS
10616.meaning: A player's pushes are held for class (P-10)

catalogRow.theySee: The bell's first row, above the list: a clock, "3 updates held until 11:50 AM" and Deliver now (52 px row, a hairline below, no tint). After Deliver now it reads "Delivered" for 2 seconds and goes. The held items are already in the list, so the row lists nothing twice. Not drawn for a coach or with nothing held

10617.name: OPENING_OR_CLEARING_A_NOTIFICATION_THE_SERVER
10617.meaning: Opening or clearing a notification: the server did not keep the read (it answered `success: false`, or the call failed)

catalogRow.theySee: An error toast, "Couldn’t mark it read" ("Couldn’t mark 3 notifications read" for a stack) + "They show as unread again. Try again."; the rows go back to unread and the error haptic plays. The panel does not stay closed over a read the server will undo on the next open

10690.name: A_ROUTE_FAILS_TO_LOAD_WHILE_THE
10690.meaning: A route fails to load (a transient or load error) while the device is offline (GAP-S-05, GAP-S-30, GAP-S-35)

catalogRow.theySee: The route error with "You’re offline" + "This page needs a connection. It loads by itself when you’re back online." and Try again (offline it says so, CH-1905, and retries nothing) with the way back to the section. Nothing retries by itself while offline; the `online` event retries once. No artificial wait before any retry: the progress shows only while the refresh runs

A banner under the top bar: "You're offline. You can keep reading and keep scoring a round; other changes need a connection." (Other saves are refused, CH-1903; only round scoring is held on the device.) When the offline queue holds anything it adds "3 changes saved on this device will sync when you reconnect." It leaves when the connection returns
catalogRow.how: `OfflineBanner`, `online`/`offline` events, `useOfflineSyncStatus().pendingCount.total` (refreshed after a queued round write), warning haptic

10702.name: A_SAVE_TAKES_LONGER_THAN_5_SECONDS
10702.meaning: A save takes longer than 5 seconds (forms, switches and CoachHelm settings)

catalogRow.theySee: "Still saving…" + "This is taking longer than usual. Keep this page open." (once per save)
"Couldn’t save your profile: you’re offline" (the action named) + "Reconnect, then try again. Nothing was changed." Nothing is sent and switches don't flip

10704.name: SOMEONE_PRESSES_TRY_AGAIN_ON_A_NOTICE
10704.meaning: Someone presses Try again on a notice, or on a page that didn't load, while offline

catalogRow.theySee: The notice (or the page, above its actions) adds "You’re offline. Reconnect, then try again." (warning haptic) and nothing is retried; the line leaves when the connection returns

10705.name: IN_THE_IPHONE_APP_PULLING_A_PHONE
10705.meaning: In the iPhone app, pulling a phone page down from its top

catalogRow.theySee: The page reads again (`router.refresh()`), keeping what is on screen until the new render lands. A pull starts only at the very top of the page, with no screen pushed, no full-screen flow, no sheet open and no scroll lock, not from the bar or a text area, and never inside an inner list that isn't at its own top; a first move up the page or sideways stays native. The app had no native refresh control, so the page draws one (owner-approved 2026-10-08, after D-43). Mobile Safari keeps its own pull: none of this runs there. Needs a physical-iPhone check (the WebView's own bounce must stay out of it)

10706.name: TWO_NOTICES_ABOUT_THE_SAME_THING_IN
10706.meaning: Two notices about the same thing in a row (Conversation muted, then Notifications back on)

catalogRow.theySee: Only the latest shows: a toast raised with the same `replace` key takes the live one's place, so contradictory notices never stack

10790.name: A_SAVE_STILL_HASNT_ANSWERED_AFTER_20
10790.meaning: A save still hasn’t answered after 20 seconds (GAP-S-31)

catalogRow.theySee: In place of "Still saving…" (CH-1902, the same `replace` key): "This is taking longer than usual" + "You can keep waiting, or cancel. Your changes are kept." + Cancel. Closing it keeps waiting, and it is offered again while the save is out

10791.name: SOMEONE_PRESSED_CANCEL_ON_CH_1990_OR
10791.meaning: Someone pressed Cancel on CH-1990, or presses Save again while that stopped save is still out

catalogRow.theySee: "Stopped waiting" + "Your changes are kept. If it saves after all, you’ll see it here."; the form keeps what was typed, the button is free again, and the late answer is told as any other (saved, or the failure with Try again). A second Save while it is still out sends nothing and says "Your last save hasn’t answered yet" + "You’ll see here when it does. Then you can save again.", so nothing is sent twice. A server action can’t be called back, so Cancel stops the waiting, not the save

10801.name: CLUBHOUSE_GATE
10801.meaning: Clubhouse renders for a coach or a player (isClubhouseFor); it is the only coach and player UI since Fairway's retirement (owner, 2026-11-14). Anyone with no dashboard role gets no Clubhouse screen, and held server actions refuse them through the same check.

10802.name: ROLE_SCOPED_NAV
10802.meaning: Each role sees only its own navigation (D-66), and an address not rebuilt for the viewer's role shows the not-rebuilt notice inside the Clubhouse frame, never another role's page or a Fairway page.

10803.name: TEAM_SWITCH_IS_A_HEAD_COACHS
10803.meaning: Only a head coach staffed on more than one team is offered the team switch (canSwitchTeams and two or more teams), the same gate setActiveTeam enforces: a coach on one team, an assistant on several, and a player see the team as a plain label, and a forged or unstaffed team id is refused by the server, so the switch can never be wider than the server's answer.

10804.name: IN_THE_IPHONE_APP_ONCE_A_LAUNCH
10804.meaning: In the iPhone app, once a launch at most, while iOS has not asked about push and the person has not answered this ask in either UI (the stored answer is shared with the current app's ask): a page has held for 4 seconds, nothing else is open or focused, and it is not round entry, onboarding or Settings

catalogRow.theySee: A bottom sheet with the bell: "Turn on notifications" + what push brings for the role (a player: "Know when your coach messages you, the schedule changes or a round review is ready, even with GolfHelm closed."; a coach: "Know when a player posts a round, messages you or answers an event, even with GolfHelm closed.") + "You can change this in Settings, under Notifications." + Not now and Turn on. Turn on: the light tap, then iOS's own prompt; allowed, the success tap and "Notifications are on"; not allowed, it closes quietly. Not now, Esc, the close button or a drag: closed, silent, never asked again. Nothing in a browser. Draft spec, no owner board: docs/clubhouse/phone/push-opt-in.md

10901.name: CHANGE_LANDED
10901.meaning: A change made through useAction that lands fires the success haptic and names itself in a toast; an action with no done line (an instant switch) shows no toast, its new position being the confirmation.

11301.name: BELL_MARK_ALL_OPTIMISTIC
11301.meaning: Mark all read clears the unread rows at once and puts them back when the write fails (with CH-1001); opening an unread notification marks it read at once.

11401.name: ROUTE_TRY_AGAIN
11401.meaning: A page that crashes shows its error view with Try again (Reload after an update), locked while it retries, the number of tries, and Back to Home.

11402.name: TOAST_RETRY
11402.meaning: Every error toast from useAction carries Retry, which runs the same action with the same arguments again.

11601.name: MOVING_TO_ANOTHER_PAGE
11601.meaning: Moving to another page, or its first load

catalogRow.theySee: A navigation changes the page while the shell stays put: on the phone it fades through (120ms out, a 120ms gap, 220ms in), and on the desktop it crossfades with no gap (120ms out and 180ms in together, owner decision 3, 2026-10-24) (owner 2026-10-01; React `ViewTransition`). Content is visible at once: the staggered section rise ended on 2026-10-01, and a refresh or in-page update never animates the page. Instant when motion is reduced or Animations is off (D-64)

11602.name: OPENING_MORE_ON_A_PHONE
11602.meaning: Opening the account sheet on a phone (the strip's Account pill; once More)

catalogRow.theySee: The sheet rises on the smooth spring (base, no bounce: it never passes its mark) over a fading scrim (260ms), and leaves on it, ending as it leaves sight; swiped shut, it leaves at the speed it was thrown (CH-1611). A fade when motion is reduced

11603.name: OPENING_THE_BELL_OR_ANY_MENU
11603.meaning: Opening the bell or any menu

catalogRow.theySee: It scales out of its button (180ms)
Slides up 10px and fades (260ms); the stack reflows. Held or thrown: CH-1614
The banner fades in and out (260ms)

11606.name: PRESSING_ANY_BUTTON_ROW_OR_TAB
11606.meaning: Pressing a key (a `.ch-btn`, or anything marked `data-ch-press`, up to 240px wide)

catalogRow.theySee: It shrinks about 6px (110ms) and springs back (280ms). Wider controls and rows press with a deeper tint instead (`--ch-ledger-row-press`), since a large surface scaling reads as a jolt; the tint waits `--ch-dur-press-delay` (50ms) after the finger lands, as a UIKit cell's highlight does, so a scroll that starts on a row never flashes it, and letting go clears it at once. The shrink is off when motion is reduced or Animations is off (D-64); the tint stays, since `RouteFrame` registers the touch listener iOS WebKit needs for `:active` whatever the motion setting
catalogRow.how: `useChPress` (`lib/press.ts`), mounted by `RouteFrame`; `.ch-lgr__row.is-link:active`, `.ch-more__row:active`. Page rows on the same tint and beat: Home's `.ch-hm-tl__a`, `.ch-hm-week__d`, `.ch-ph-pg button` and `a.ch-hm-next` (a deeper green), and Stats' `.ch-stm-row`, `.ch-spm-more` and `.ch-gm-how > summary`

11607.name: THE_FIRST_TAB_ON_A_PAGE
11607.meaning: The first Tab on a page

catalogRow.theySee: Skip to content slides into view (180ms)

11608.name: ANIMATIONS_OFF_IN_SETTINGS_OR_THE_OS
11608.meaning: Animations off in Settings, or the OS asks for reduced motion

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing slides, scales or springs. Under the OS setting a page or a sheet fades instead, over the quick beat (180ms), as iOS does (owner decision 2, OQ-15); Animations off makes every Clubhouse transition instant

11609.name: A_PAGE_OR_SECTION_IS_LOADING
11609.meaning: A page or section is loading

catalogRow.theySee: The skeleton fades in (260ms) as soon as it mounts (`--ch-skel-delay` is 0 since F-37); one shimmer sweep shared by every block (1.9s loop), a shade deeper than the parchment. On desktop Ledger pages a block placeholder (fluid, 56px or taller) is a rule with two lines of type, never a filled card; a real object asks for `shape="solid"`. They hold still when Animations is off or motion is reduced (D-64)

11610.name: A_PHONE_SCREEN_IS_PUSHED_OR_POPPED
11610.meaning: A phone screen is pushed (a thread, details, a new message) or popped

catalogRow.theySee: It slides in from the right on the smooth spring (base, no bounce: it never passes the left edge), and back out over the base ease-out, so the page beneath is free again at once; settles immediately with reduced motion. A Back that iOS already animated leaves at once (CH-1908). The page beneath draws back and dims with it (CH-1618). The underlying page keeps its scroll position through nested screens and exit, and focus returns without scrolling

11611.name: SOMEONE_DRAGS_A_PHONE_SHEET_DOWN_BY
11611.meaning: Someone drags a phone sheet (More, the bell, any `Modal`, and the pages' own sheets) by its grab or header, or by its body once that is scrolled to the top

catalogRow.theySee: It follows the finger. Pulled up past its open position it gives like a UIKit rubber band (never more than 100px) over a floor of its own colour, so no gap opens under it. Past 80px or on a quick flick it closes with the medium settle haptic (D-70) and leaves at the speed it was thrown, on the smooth spring; otherwise it springs back on the smooth spring from the speed it was moving; thrown back up hard it carries on a little past its open position over the same floor, and a finger can catch it on the way where it is. The coach chat's history drawer stops at its open edge instead: thrown back too hard to stop there from its speed, it starts slower, so it never passes the edge. From the body a drag starts only after a 6px move whose first direction is down, never within 100ms of a scroll and never from a field; a scroll, a sideways move or a tap stays the body's, and the row a drag started on doesn't open. With reduced motion there is no drag: the sheet fades, and Close, the scrim and Esc close it. The Close button inside stays a button. A single primary pointer owns the drag; another finger cannot replace it, and cancellation springs back. Nested and exiting overlays retain the shared background scroll lock. The body drag and the claim of a downward move at the top need a physical-iPhone check
catalogRow.how: `useSheetDrag` (`lib/sheet-drag.ts`) in `TabBar`, `Bell`, `Modal` and the page sheets; `takeSheetFling` into `lib/dialog-lifetime.ts` and the More and bell exits

11612.name: OPENING_THE_BELL_ON_A_PHONE
11612.meaning: Opening the bell on a phone

catalogRow.theySee: The notifications sheet rises on the smooth spring over a fading scrim (260ms) and leaves on it, as More does (CH-1602); a fade when motion is reduced

The selected plate glides to the tapped row on the first frame of the tap, on the smooth spring (base, no bounce), and the rows' ink follows at the base pace; a second tap mid-glide sends it on from where it is at the speed it is going, except toward a row too near to stop at from that speed: there it starts slower, so it never passes the row. It lands without travelling on first paint and on resize, and jumps with reduced motion. Without script each row draws its own plate
catalogRow.how: `NavPlate` (the spring sampled into Web Animations keyframes), `.ch-nav__plate`

11614.name: A_FINGER_HOLDS_A_TOAST_OR_THROWS
11614.meaning: A finger holds a toast, or throws it

catalogRow.theySee: Held, its clock stops; let go, it finishes what was left, and stays at least 1.5 seconds. Thrown toward the edge its stack sits on (down at the foot of the screen, up when it drops from the top inside a sheet, CH-1812), past 40px or on a flick it goes on at the speed it was thrown and fades; short of that it springs back; the other way it barely gives. Its action stays a button. No haptic. With reduced motion it doesn't follow the finger, but holding it still stops its clock
The raised chip slides to it on the settle spring (base, bounce 0.1: it passes its mark by about 0.15%, under a pixel); at once with reduced motion or Animations off

11616.name: CONTENT_SWAPS_INSIDE_A_FIXED_FRAME
11616.meaning: Content swaps inside a fixed frame (a tab's panel, a chart's mode, a window's figures, a pager)

catalogRow.theySee: The incoming copy fades in over base and travels its 6px rise or 12px slide on the settle spring; the outgoing fades over quick; nothing on first paint; at once with reduced motion or Animations off

11617.name: PRESSING_A_SEGMENTED_CONTROLS_OPTION_OR_A
11617.meaning: Pressing a segmented control's option or a pill that isn't on, or the kit's feature card as a link or a button

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing scales (CH-1606): the option or pill takes the press tint (`--ch-ledger-row-press`) over the press beat (110ms), the card a shade over its green, each after the 50ms beat a UIKit cell waits, so a scroll that starts on one never flashes it; letting go clears it at once, and the chip slides to a new choice (CH-1615). The chosen option and a pill that is on don't answer: there is nothing to change. The tint stays with reduced motion, since it isn't motion; Animations off makes it instant

11618.name: THE_PAGE_BENEATH_A_PHONE_SCREEN_AS
11618.meaning: The page beneath a phone screen as the screen is pushed or popped (a thread, details, a profile, a prospect, a read)

catalogRow.theySee: The page beneath draws back about a quarter of the width and dims under a light warm scrim as the screen slides in, on the screen's own smooth spring, and comes back with it over the base ease-out as it pops. The two edges move as one, frame by frame, so no gap opens between them, and a pop that cuts a push short reverses both from where they are. The top bar and the tab bar go with the page, and stay on screen over a page scrolled down. A screen with another pushed over it draws back and dims the same way. A Back that iOS animated itself, or a screen gone with its page, puts the page back at once. With reduced motion or Animations off the page holds still. Owner-approved 2026-10-08. WebKit at 390, 2026-10-08: the page lands at −94px (24% of 390), within a pixel of 0.24 times the screen's travel on every sampled frame
catalogRow.how: `PhoneUnderlay` and `usePhonePushed` (shell/phone-chrome.tsx: the scrim's opacity drives the page), `PhoneScreen` (`covered`), `.ch-pscrim` and `.ch-pscreen[data-ch-covered]::after` (shell.css); the scroll lock clips the body rather than hiding it (lib/overlay-scroll.ts)

11619.name: A_PAGE_ARRIVES_IN_PLACE_OF_ITS
11619.meaning: A page arrives in place of its route skeleton after a navigation

catalogRow.theySee: It fades in over the press beat (110ms, opacity only; nothing moves), so the swap settles instead of cutting. A skeleton marked `data-ch-arrive="crossfade"` (the CoachHelm read, READ-S4) crossfades with the page over the quick beat (180ms) instead. The fade holds at its first frame until the page has painted, so a busy first frame never uses it up. Never on the first paint of a server-rendered page, never again on a refresh or an update inside the page, and not with reduced motion or Animations off. Owner-approved 2026-10-08
catalogRow.how: `useSkeletonReveal` in `RouteFrame` (a route skeleton is `main[aria-busy='true'][aria-label^='Loading']`, as base.css marks it)

11620.name: A_FINGER_OR_THE_POINTER_HOLDS_A
11620.meaning: A finger or the pointer holds a switch

catalogRow.theySee: Its thumb stretches about a fifth of its width toward where it would travel (19 to 22.8px; Settings' rows 27 to 32.4px), as UISwitch's does, growing from the edge it rests on, and settles round as it slides across on release. It uses the scale property, so nothing reflows. A disabled or saving switch doesn't stretch. Off with reduced motion and with Animations off, as the press is. Owner-approved 2026-10-08
catalogRow.how: `.ch-switch:active .ch-switch__thumb` (controls.css; the track is a size container, so the thumb finds the track's inner edge at any size)

11621.name: SCROLLING_THE_DESKTOP_CANVAS_WITH_A_MAC
11621.meaning: Scrolling the desktop canvas with a Mac trackpad

catalogRow.theySee: It scrolls natively, on the trackpad's own momentum, never eased a second time; a glide a notched wheel started stops where it is when the fingers take over. A notched wheel still eases (`CH_SCROLL_DUR`). Off the Mac every wheel eases, as before. Owner-approved 2026-10-08. Telling the two apart needs a check with a real trackpad and mouse

11622.name: PULLING_A_PHONE_PAGE_DOWN_FROM_ITS
11622.meaning: Pulling a phone page down from its top, in the iPhone app (CH-1909)

catalogRow.theySee: The parchment sheet comes down off the green chassis with UIKit's rubber band, and the spinner's spokes come in one by one; past 64px they turn in eighths with a fading tail. Let go, the sheet settles at the spinner (52px) on the smooth spring from the finger's speed, and springs home once the read has landed (and the spinner has shown for the reveal beat); short of the trigger it springs home. A finger can catch it on the way. Reduced motion and Animations off settle at once, and the spinner holds still. Owner-approved 2026-10-08

11701.name: CHANGING_TABS
11701.meaning: Changing section (a strip pill or a committed swipe on the bar; not the section they're on)

11704.name: OPENING_MORE_SWIPING_THE_SHEET_AWAY
11704.meaning: Opening the account sheet; swiping it away

catalogRow.theySee: A tick; a medium tap as the sheet settles shut (D-70)

11705.name: OPENING_THE_BELL_A_NOTIFICATION_OR_A
11705.meaning: Opening the bell, a notification, or a menu item

The OS warning pattern

11707.meaning: Picking another team in the switcher

11709.name: A_PULL_TO_REFRESH_PASSES_ITS_TRIGGER
11709.meaning: A pull to refresh passes its trigger (the iPhone app, CH-1909)

catalogRow.theySee: The medium tap, once (D-70's settle; owner-approved for the pull 2026-10-08)

11801.name: THE_FIRST_TAB_ON_ANY_PAGE_OFFERS
11801.meaning: The first Tab on any page offers "Skip to content", which jumps past the navigation to the page

11802.name: THE_PHONE_MORE_SHEET_IS_MODAL_FOCUS
11802.meaning: The phone account sheet (the section strip's last pill; once the More sheet) is modal: focus moves in without scrolling, Tab stays inside, Esc closes it and focus returns to the section title without scrolling. It holds who you are, the coach's team switch, Help and Sign out. The underlying page stays stationary until the full exit completes

11803.name: THE_CURRENT_PAGE_IS_MARKED_IN_THE
11803.meaning: The current page is marked in the sidebar and tab bar; the sidebar and its navigation are named landmarks; breadcrumbs mark the current page

11804.name: TOASTS_ARE_ANNOUNCED_CONFIRMATIONS_POLITELY_ERRORS_RIGHT
11804.meaning: Toasts are announced: confirmations politely, errors right away

11805.name: THE_BELL_PANEL_IS_A_DIALOG_IT
11805.meaning: The bell panel is a dialog: it takes focus on open, Esc closes it, and the filter menu works by keyboard

catalogRow.test: shell.test › CH-1805 (opens as a dialog); preview (keyboard)

11806.name: EVERY_CONTROL_SHOWS_A_FOCUS_RING_ON
11806.meaning: Every control shows a focus ring on keyboard focus; text fields show their own green or ink ring instead, never two

catalogRow.how: `base.css` `:focus-visible`; on the phone's green hero the bell's champagne ring, 2px off its disc (`shell.css`)

11807.name: NO_AXE_VIOLATIONS_WITH_THE_BELL_OPEN
11807.meaning: No axe violations (WCAG 2.2 AA, contrast included) with the bell open (a sheet on the phone) and the More sheet open

11808.name: THE_PHONE_TAB_BAR_LISTS_THE_ROLES
11808.meaning: The phone section strip (section-strip.md) lists the role's sections, the old tabs first (coach: Home, CoachHelm, Calendar, Stats; player: Home, CoachHelm, Rounds, Team Hub; D-66), then the sidebar's order, then Settings and the Account pill; the current one is `aria-current`; a pill with a count is named with it ("Messages 3 new"). Shut, it is hidden and inert

11809.name: A_PUSHED_PHONE_SCREEN_IS_NAMED_BY
11809.meaning: A pushed phone screen is named by its title, and focus moves to that title; while it is up, the shell's top bar and tab bar are inert, so VoiceOver can't wander behind it

11810.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_TOP_BAR_NAMES
11810.meaning: On the phone the top bar names the page; a page with its own top (`PhoneTop`) gets a back link named for where it goes ("Back to More") in place of the bell

11811.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_BELL_OPENS_AS
11811.meaning: On the phone the bell drops the feed as lock-screen stacks under a green veil (`BellStacks`, notification-stacks.ts) instead of a popover: a modal dialog; focus moves in, Tab stays inside, Esc, a tap on the open space, the bell or a drag up closes it and focus returns to the bell; the edge swipe is off while it is up

11812.name: A_TOAST_RAISED_WHILE_A_DIALOG_OR
11812.meaning: A toast raised while a dialog or sheet is open shows inside it (on the phone, from the top), so it is seen, announced and its Retry can be tapped; a modal dialog makes everything outside it inert, which had hidden them. When the dialog closes, open toasts move back to the page

11813.name: ON_A_DESKTOP_A_HEAD_COACH_ON
11813.meaning: On a desktop a head coach on more than one team sees the sidebar's Team group heading (the team's name) as a menu button (the boards' up-down chevrons): it opens a listbox of the teams with the current one `aria-selected`; arrows, Home and End move, Enter or Space picks, Esc or Tab closes and focus returns to the button; a pick switches at once and every screen re-reads for the new team

11814.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_SAME_COACH_SEES
11814.meaning: On the phone the same coach sees their teams in the account sheet, under who they are, the current one marked (`aria-current`); a switch closes the sheet on the new team, a refused one leaves it open with the reason

11815.name: ON_THE_PHONE_EVERY_KEY_A_FINGER
11815.meaning: On the phone every key a finger uses reaches at least 44 by 44: the bar's back link and text action (a pushed screen's bar has the shell bar's 44px row, with no hairline), the hero bell (its 40px disc drawn inside a 44px key, where it was), a sheet's Close (its reach leans up into the header's padding, so a title-only header no longer clips it to 43), and the search field (36px drawn, 44px to the finger; its input and clear key take their own taps, and its 16px text keeps iOS from zooming the page on focus). Measured in WebKit at 390 on 2026-10-08

11816.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_DOCK_THE_BAND
11816.meaning: On the phone the dock, the band just above the tab bar, carries a page's primary controls (`ThumbDock`) and the Resume round accessory; it hides with the tab bar (a pushed screen, a full-page form) and while a field has focus (the keyboard), and the canvas grows by its height so the last row clears it. Empty, it is not drawn

11817.name: ON_THE_PHONE_WHILE_THE_PLAYER_HAS
11817.meaning: On the phone, while the player has a round in progress (touched in the last 12 hours), a parchment accessory above the tab bar reads “Round in progress, Oakmont CC · Hole 7”; one tap opens the shot screen. Not shown on the round's own screens or for a round whose screen isn't rebuilt

11818.name: ON_A_DESKTOP_THE_SIDEBARS_CARD_SLOT
11818.meaning: On a desktop the sidebar's card slot resumes the player's round in progress in place of the next event

11819.name: ON_A_TOUCH_SCREEN_HOLDING_A_PEEKABLE
11819.meaning: On a touch screen, holding a peekable object (a player's name) for about 450ms ticks once and raises its card over the dimmed, softened page where the row was, its actions listed under it (the native context menu's anatomy); the tap the hold ends with does not open the row, a scroll or drag past 8px cancels the hold, and iOS's link callout stays out of it. Esc, a tap outside or an action closes it, but not the lift that ends the hold; focus returns to the row

11820.name: ON_A_DESKTOP_RESTING_THE_POINTER_ON
11820.meaning: On a desktop, resting the pointer on it for 400ms (or focusing it from the keyboard for 600ms) opens a hover card beside it with the same actions as small keys; leaving the target and the card, Esc, or a scroll that moves the target closes it

11821.name: THE_PLAYER_PEEK_NAME_AND_CLASS_WHY
11821.meaning: The player peek: name and class, why they need a look (ink, the amber on its icon), the last round, the average and a word-sized line of the last scores; Message opens Messages with the player as the recipient (never sends), View stats and Plan 1:1 open their pages, and CoachHelm the player's deep dive (`coachhelm?view=deep-dive&player=`, not drawn until CoachHelm is rebuilt for coaches). Wired on Home's leaderboard; other pages wrap their names in `PlayerPeek`

11822.name: A_COACHS_TOP_BAR_CARRIES_AN_ASK
11822.meaning: Retired 2026-11-15 (the quick chat replaced the Ask key and its sheet; OVL-19). A coach's top bar carries an Ask key (desktop and phone; only while CoachHelm is on for the coach, not on CoachHelm itself, and never for a player): it opens the Ask sheet over the page

11823.name: THE_ASK_SHEET_IS_COACHHELMS_ASK_OVER
11823.meaning: Retired 2026-11-15 (the quick chat replaced the Ask key and its sheet, and the unused sheet body was deleted; OVL-19). The Ask sheet is CoachHelm's Ask over any screen: the same chat hook and route (no new model or spend), the thread and the message box, saved like any chat; Open in CoachHelm goes to it there. Phone: a bottom sheet that opens at half height with the page in view and grows to full when a thread starts (the grab or the chevron toggles); desktop: a centred sheet. Its heading takes focus, Esc, Close or the backdrop close it, and a new page (or another player) closes it and starts the next one fresh; in the app it sits above the keyboard

11824.name: THE_SHEET_NAMES_WHAT_THE_COACH_IS
11824.meaning: The sheet names what the coach is looking at (“Looking at: Stats · Jonah Okafor”, from the page's trail or the navigation); a page about one player (`?player=`) also hands the chat that player as its context chip

11825.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_SECTIONS_NAME_IN
11825.meaning: On the phone the section's name in the top bar is the section switcher: a button with a chevron (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls="ch-strip"`) that opens the section strip, with a dot and a spoken note while another section has something new; on a section's own page a pull down on the bar draws the strip and a sideways swipe steps to the next section

11826.name: A_TOAST_IS_CLOSED_WITHOUT_A_FINGER
11826.meaning: A toast is closed without a finger: on a device with a mouse (`hover: hover`) it has a ghost Dismiss X ("Dismiss notification"), and Esc closes it while focus is inside it. Focus goes back where it was before it came into the toast; inside an open dialog (CH-1812) Esc closes only the toast. Closing it counts as letting it run out: held work (a calendar move, CH-6015) is written

11827.name: THE_RESUME_ROUND_ACCESSORY_CARRIES_A_DISCARD
11827.meaning: The Resume round accessory carries a discard control (×) beside Resume (owner, 2026-10-31: “let me discard it”). It opens CH-1824; nothing is deleted on the tap

11828.name: DISCARDING_FROM_THE_ACCESSORY_ASKS_THE_SCORECARDS
11828.meaning: Discarding from the accessory asks the scorecard's question (CH-11515, “Discard this round?”, with the round's course and hole). Confirmed, it deletes the round on the server, then clears this device's copy, marks it discarded and drops its queued submit, and the shell reads again so the accessory goes; a refusal keeps everything and says why (CH-11009)

11901.name: PHONE_CHROME
11901.meaning: On a phone the sidebar gives way to the section strip: the role's first sections (coach Home, CoachHelm, Calendar, Stats; player Home, CoachHelm, Rounds, Team Hub), then the rest in sidebar order, then Settings, each only once its screen is rebuilt for the role. There is no bottom tab bar.

12001.name: ON_THE_PHONE_THE_EDGE_SWIPE_OR
12001.meaning: On the phone, the edge swipe or the browser's back while a screen is pushed

catalogRow.theySee: The top screen pops, as the back link would; the page stays put

12002.name: ON_THE_PHONE_TAPPING_THE_TAB_THAT
12002.meaning: On the phone, tapping the strip's pill for the section already open

catalogRow.theySee: What a UIKit tab bar does: a pushed screen or section pops back to the tab's root (through history, CH-1906); a page below the tab's root goes back up to it; at the root the page scrolls to the top, smoothly (at once with reduced motion). No tick (CH-1701)

12003.name: ON_IOS_A_BACK_THAT_SAFARI_OR
12003.meaning: On iOS, a Back that Safari or the app's WebView animated itself (the edge swipe; `PopStateEvent.hasUAVisualTransition`, Safari 18 and later)

catalogRow.theySee: The Back shows once: a pushed screen leaves at once instead of sliding out again, and the page crossfade doesn't run after it. Elsewhere the flag never arrives and nothing changes. Needs a physical-iPhone check (Safari and the app)

12101.name: THE_PAGE_IS_SLOW_TO_RESPOND_OR
12101.meaning: The page is slow to respond or shifts after loading (INP, CLS, LCP)

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing on screen

12201.name: SOMEONE_CLICKS_THE_SAME_THING_OVER_AND
12201.meaning: Someone clicks the same thing over and over (rage click)

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing on screen
catalogRow.how: Sentry Replay in production. Partial: only 10% of sessions are recorded, plus every session that has an error, so most rage clicks are not seen. No Clubhouse-side detector yet

12202.name: A_CLICK_THAT_DOES_NOTHING
12202.meaning: A click that does nothing (dead click)

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing on screen
catalogRow.how: Sentry Replay, same 10% plus error sessions

12203.name: A_SLOW_RESPONSE_TO_A_CLICK
12203.meaning: A slow response to a click (slow click)

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing on screen
catalogRow.how: Sentry Replay, same 10% plus error sessions

12301.name: FAILURES_REPORTED
12301.meaning: A thrown action is reported through chReport with its surface and action; a refused one at low severity; every event is tagged ui=clubhouse, and server reads log through chLogServer as clubhouse.<surface>.{read}.

12401.name: TESTS_NAME_CONTRACTS
12401.meaning: Every catalog code is used in code and forced by a test that names it; clubhouse:check fails a row of kinds 0 to 5 that no test names.

20101.name: COACH_HOME_READY
20101.meaning: Coach Home opens with the date, the greeting and the brief, Up next beside the hero, Today and the team's scoring form, the team's four parts and the latest round, all read on the server for the first paint; a team with nothing yet gets the first-run page. The leaderboard and the week are not on Home (Roster, Stats and Calendar).

20102.name: PLAYER_HOME_READY
20102.meaning: Player Home opens with the date and the greeting (no brief line: owner, 2026-10-06), Message coach, the week beside Up next and Your latest round in one sheet, then Scoring and the four parts of the game, all read on the server for the first paint; a new player gets the first-run page (CH-2312), and on a phone the same data is drawn as the phone Home (21901).

20103.name: LINKS_OPEN_WHAT_THEY_NAME
20103.meaning: Every link out of Home opens the thing it names: Message team the team chat (?conversation=) or Messages when the chat did not load, Up next and a Today row that event in Calendar (?date=&event=), or a trip with no event of its own that trip on Team Hub's Travel (/golf/dashboard/team-hub?tab=travel&trip=), and Up next's "Nothing else this week" card the next event or trip it names, a week day Calendar's day view (?view=day&date=), New event, Plan, Add event and the quick event types the editor (?new=1, with &type=), a leaderboard row and a latest round's stats link that player's stats (?player=), My stats the player's own stats, Message coach the coach's thread (?user=), the first run's Invite players Roster with its invite sheet open (/golf/dashboard/roster?invite=1), each part of the coach's "Waiting on you" the screen that holds it (join requests Roster, replies that event in Calendar when one event holds them and Calendar when more do, overdue tasks Team Hub's Tasks ?tab=tasks, posts awaiting acknowledgement its Announcements ?tab=ann), a name in the team's four parts that player's Game tab on Stats on the same Last 10 (?player=&tab=game) and Team stats Stats, the coach's Next row Nudge Messages prefilled for who hasn't replied (the phone day card's own link, never sent), and CoachHelm in the player peek and the phone's round sheet that player's deep dive (/golf/dashboard/coachhelm?view=deep-dive&player=); a link to a screen not yet rebuilt for the viewer's role is not drawn.

20104.name: COACH_QUEUE_COUNTS_AS_ITS_SCREEN
20104.meaning: Coach Home's "Waiting on you" (under the head on desktop, in the phone's hero, and on the first run) counts each part with the read and rule of the screen that holds it, so the two show one number: pending join requests as the sidebar's Roster badge counts them, replies missing on this week's events that still take one as Team Hub's RSVPs count "no reply" (rsvpQueue), overdue tasks as Team Hub's Tasks (taskStatus, overdueTaskCount) and posts awaiting an acknowledgement as its Announcements (unackedPostCount). Only parts above zero are drawn, in that order; with nothing waiting the row is not drawn. Each part reads on its own: one that fails is null, logged and left out, never 0 (CH-2220).

20105.name: TEAM_PARTS_ON_THE_FORMS_LAST_10
20105.meaning: Coach Home's four parts (The team's game; under the team's form on desktop, after Team scoring on the phone) read the form's own Last 10 rounds of the active roster, hole-level only (Q-123): strokes gained per round in each part is Team Stats' own team figure (teamStrokesGained): the rounds of the players who have 3 rounds with strokes gained in that window, so a player's first round or two moves it neither here nor on Stats (no player at that floor: none), its change against the same players' previous ten (Q-112) coloured only when it clears its standard error, the part's plain stat (Fairways, Greens, Up and down, Putts) with the Tour's mark from the team's tour, and who gains and loses most from Team Stats' ranking (ties share a place and are named together; one ranked player, or everyone in one place, loses nothing). No other player's round reaches the figures.

catalogRow.theySee: A skeleton in Home's own shape (header, two panes, five leaderboard rows), so nothing shifts when data lands. On the phone the hero is the reader's own, from the shell's role: the coach's brief as three lines over the coach's Up next card, the player's Up next with its countdown under the greeting and the two keys under it; the card, the keys and the first section land within half a pixel of their bars (WebKit 390, 2026-10-08)

20202.name: THE_SHEET_OPENS_BEFORE_THE_CLASS_DAY
20202.meaning: The sheet opens before the class day has arrived

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing for 300 ms, then a small spinner and "Loading class status"

20301.name: CLOCK_KEEPS_TIME
20301.meaning: The phone's Up next line (In 50 min, Happening now) is recomputed from the device clock every minute, so it needs no reload.

"No 18-hole rounds posted yet this season." + "6 players are on the roster. The leaderboard fills in as rounds are posted." With no round at all, the one line that says so on desktop (the latest round's pane steps aside)

20406.name: A_PLAYER_HAS_FEWER_THAN_THREE_ROUNDS
20406.meaning: A player has fewer than three rounds

20407.name: A_COACH_WITH_NO_ACTIVE_TEAM
20407.meaning: A coach with no active team

catalogRow.theySee: The page empty state (v2 medallion): "You aren’t on a team yet" + what Home shows once they are + Open team settings (Team)

20408.name: A_TEAM_WITH_NOTHING_YET_NO_PLAYERS
20408.meaning: A team with nobody on it yet: no players, no rounds, and every read answered (events or not: it rests on the people, not the calendar)

catalogRow.theySee: The v2 page empty state (gh-states.jsx `EMPTY.home.coach`, D-71): "Your season starts here" + "Add your players and your first event…" ("Add your players." once there is an event) Invite players (Roster's invite sheet) and New event (Calendar's editor); the header's actions step aside. With events this week, the week sits above it (desktop: the week pane; phone: the week strip). It opens under the loaded page's framed head on desktop (the date and the greeting where the loaded Home sets them) and under the Ledger's page intro on the phone (states audit, 2026-10-08)

20409.name: NOTHING_ON_THE_CALENDAR_AHEAD
20409.meaning: Nothing on the calendar ahead, this week or after it: no event and no trip (phone). A player: "Your coach’s practices and events will show here with a countdown.", no quick adds

catalogRow.theySee: Up next reads "No events scheduled" + what the card will hold, with Practice, Qualifier, Tournament and Meeting (each opens the editor on that type, `?new=1&type=`) and Add event. The week strip steps aside. With something after this week, CH-2316 instead

20410.name: FEWER_THAN_TWO_18_HOLE_ROUNDS
20410.meaning: Fewer than two 18-hole rounds (player Home Scoring)

catalogRow.theySee: "One round so far." or "No rounds posted yet this season." + "Your scoring line starts with your second 18-hole round."

20411.name: NO_FAIRWAYS_GREENS_SCRAMBLING_OR_PUTTS_LOGGED
20411.meaning: No fairways, greens, scrambling or putts logged (player Home)

catalogRow.theySee: "Nothing to break down yet." + "Fairways, greens, scrambling and putts fill in from rounds posted with those stats."

20412.name: A_NEW_PLAYER_NO_ROUNDS_NOTHING_ON
20412.meaning: A new player: no rounds, every read answered (v2 first-run, D-71)

catalogRow.theySee: Nothing on the calendar: the page empty state "Welcome to the team" + "Post your first round to start your stats. Team updates and your schedule show up here too." (it names the head's New round; without round entry, "Your stats start with the first round you post. …") with Add classes only stands in for Your latest round, Scoring and Your game

20413.name: A_PLAYER_ON_NO_ACTIVE_TEAM
20413.meaning: A player on no active team

catalogRow.theySee: "You aren’t on a team yet" + "Ask your coach for your team’s code or an invite. Once you join, Home shows your week, your rounds and your stats." + Open team settings (Golf profile, where joining lives, CH-8302)

20414.name: NO_ROUND_IN_THE_TEAMS_LAST_10
20414.meaning: No round in the team's last 10 has hole scores (coach Home, the team's four parts)

catalogRow.theySee: "No hole-by-hole rounds in the last 10 yet." + "The four parts fill in once players post rounds with hole scores." in place of the ledger, under its head

20415.name: ROUNDS_WITH_HOLE_SCORES_BUT_NO_PLAYER
20415.meaning: Rounds with hole scores, but no player with 3 of them (coach Home, the team's four parts)

catalogRow.theySee: The parts and their figures stay; Gains most and Loses most read "—", and under the ledger "No player has 3 rounds with hole scores yet, so no one is ranked."

20416.name: NOBODY_ON_THE_TEAM_HAS_A_CLASS
20416.meaning: Nobody on the team has a class today (the sheet is open)

catalogRow.theySee: Title "No classes today", sub "9 players · Class names show to coaches only.", the strip hidden, "No one has a class today."; Travelling and No class status still list

20417.name: NOTHING_LEFT_THIS_WEEK_BUT_AN_EVENT
